analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials 11.9.26-11.13.26 Weekend Edition
key_insights: Industrials rose 350bps on the week and materials rose 50bps. The broader market rose 230bps, led by energy, with housing lagging on higher rates.

Small and mid cap AI-linked names led. MOD rose 43% (30% on Friday on takeout headlines), AAON rose 40% after a beat, and CECO rose 26% after guiding 2027 well ahead of expectations. LGN, AVEX, FLY, DPC and HAWK also gained on earnings.
CTVA fell 22% on a sharply lower implied Q4 outlook with earnings, and FMC fell 10% in tandem. GFL fell 9% after its Board ended the sale process and said it will stay standalone.
Housing-related names DFH, LGIH, NX, HOV and NVR were weak after a surprise rise in rates following US CPI.

Prime Services data show hedge funds net sold US equities for a second straight week. Single Stocks were heavily net sold, with short sales driving it and long flows muted. Macro Products (index and ETFs) were net bought for a third straight week, on short covers and long buys.
US Info Tech was the most net sold sector again. Its long/short ratio is 1.5, versus a YTD peak of 2.14 in early June and the lowest on record (since 2016).

Momentum exposure in the Prime Book is at multi-year lows (23rd percentile over 5 years). The most crowded longs in the space are URI, WAB, PH, XPO and AME, and the most crowded shorts are UPS, ITW, GWW, DE and OTIS.

WWD reports fiscal Q4 on Wednesday 11/17 after the close (call at 5pm) and is expected to guide 2027. The options market implies a 9% move. The stock fell 8% last quarter but was up on five of the last six reports, and the desk calls guidance events 50/50.

WWD consensus has full-year EPS growth slowing from 38% to 13% on revenue up 9% versus 22% in fiscal 2026. Buyside expectations are in line with consensus, and the mix across business lines will matter.

WWD has lagged aerospace peers over the last month (roughly flat versus high single digit gains in HEI, TDG and GE). It trades at 20x EBITDA versus 26-27x earlier this year, and at 30x P/E versus 40x+. The stock sits on its 50-day average, with a breakout above $365 on a better guide or a retrace to $300 on a worse one. The desk rates crowding 6/10 and sees the print as a possible clearing event to bring buyers back.

HWM CFO meeting: aerospace demand remains strong and price is expected to be an enduring theme. HWM expects each capacity addition to drive share gain and sees further volume upside from added scope. Engine Products carry a 39% adjusted EBITDA margin, and about 90% of their sales are under long-term agreements.

HWM Fastening Systems has a lower long-term-agreement mix. Margins are diluted by the CAM acquisition, which runs at about 20% adjusted EBITDA margin. Management expects to lift CAM margins closer to 30% within two years.

HWM targets about $2.5bn of industrial gas turbine (IGT) revenue by 2030, driven by data center buildouts and rising electricity demand. IGT demand is shifting to H-class and newer turbines with more HWM content. HWM has taken price every year since 2019, and generators in data centers strain turbines, which may mean more replacements.

HWM capital allocation: the first wave of capacity build-out covers the next 3-4 years, with capex staying elevated through 2028 at about 5-6% of revenue. Beyond capex, priorities are M&A, share repurchases and the dividend. HWM reads recent industry strategic action as a sign of a constrained supply environment, not new direct competition.

HEI site visit: PMA (FAA-approved alternative parts) development takes from a month for simple parts to several months for complex ones. HEI can repair components cheaper and faster than the original manufacturer using in-house PMA parts.

HEI has had solid double-digit organic growth across aerospace and defense, OE and aftermarket, though quarterly growth is lumpy. Incremental margins in several recent quarters exceeded the historical average. HEI prices existing products below industry levels, but prices new contracts and products at market, and new products are more profitable.
HEI sees a large pool of A&D supply chain M&A. Competition is higher for businesses with sole-source, high-IP pricing power, and HEI says it remains a disciplined buyer.

Next week's macro calendar includes Retail Sales, Industrial Production, Housing Starts, FOMC Minutes and NVDA earnings, plus WMT, HD, LOW and TGT results. Off-cycle earnings from WWD, ACM, VIK and KEYS are in focus, along with analyst days at BLDR, ECL, GXO, EXPD, ROK and MOD.

WWD stock fell 8% after last quarter's report and has risen on five of the last six reports.
CECO rose 26% on the week after guiding 2027 well ahead of expectations, and AAON rose 40% on the week after an earnings beat (no figures given).

US-listed ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest covering in 7 months, led by Large Cap Equity, Credit and Tech ETFs.

Single Stocks were net sold at -1.7 SDs over 1 year, and 8 of 11 sectors were net sold. Info Tech, Financials, Health Care and Staples led the selling, while Consumer Discretionary, Energy and Real Estate were net bought.
